rows.description: After being lied to many times, you trust no news at all. Total distrust is as manipulable as blind trust. Keep a small set of sources with track records of corrections, and hold conclusions loosely.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, deceit, dependence, guilt, manipulation, trust

rows.description: You use AI for every email, idea and decision and feel your own skills fading. Use it as a collaborator: draft first yourself, check its claims, and keep skills sharp. Convenience is fine, but outsourcing all thinking dulls you.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, envy, fear, honesty, loneliness, trust

rows.description: The answers are fluent and confident, and you accept them. Fluency is not accuracy. Verify facts, code, and legal or medical advice with reliable sources and people. Trust tools in proportion to how easily you can check them.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, dependence, envy, fear, honesty, loneliness

rows.description: You worry AI will make your career obsolete. Take it seriously and act: learn the tools, focus on judgment, relationships and domain depth, and keep upskilling. Panic or denial both waste the time you have.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, dependence, envy, honesty, loneliness, trust

rows.description: Chatting with AI feels easier than with people because it never judges. It can help you rehearse and reflect, but does not replace friends who know you, disagree and need you back. Keep human bonds alive.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, dependence, envy, fear, honesty, trust

rows.description: Coworkers accuse you of cheating because you use AI well. Be open about how you use it, take responsibility for the output, and help others learn. Skill lies in framing problems and checking results.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, dependence, fear, honesty, loneliness, trust

rows.description: Your boss expects doubled output because AI exists. Show what it can and cannot do, protect review time, and flag risks such as errors and confidential data. Honest expectations serve both of you better than silent overwork.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: dependence, envy, fear, honesty, loneliness, trust

rows.description: You are tempted to pass AI work off as fully your own in a place where that is not allowed. Follow the rules, disclose when required, and understand what you submit. Being caught is less costly than lacking the competence you claimed.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, dependence, envy, fear, loneliness, trust

rows.description: A junior copies AI output without understanding it. Ask them to explain the reasoning, review together, and teach them to verify. Guiding good use is better than banning it, and it prepares them for a workplace shaped by AI.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, dependence, envy, fear, honesty, loneliness

rows.subtopic: Moving abroad or to a new city
rows.description: In a new city or country, you miss home food, language and easy jokes. Loneliness is normal at first. Join clubs, meet colleagues outside work, keep calls with family, and give yourself months, not weeks, to belong.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, exploitation, guilt, prejudice
